newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Crystallex unfazed by CVG court case.
newsitem.headline: Crystallex unfazed by CVG court case.

text.p: Canadian mining company Crystallex International Corp said it was unfazed by Venezuelan state-holding company Corporacion Venezolana de Guayana's (CVG) reported decision to sue the company for damages related to delays in the gold rich Las Cristinas gold project.

The CVG is partner with Canadian gold major Placer Dome in the $600 million Las Cristinas project that has recently blown-up into a raging legal battle following claims by Crystallex that it owns the concession.
"I don't think that (the CVG case) is of any concern to us," Crystallex Vice President Richard Marshall told Reuters.
A flurry of market rumors followed news of the CVG suit, reported in the national press Monday.

CVG officials were not immediately available to confirm the reports and CVG lawyers declined comment. But Placer spokesperson Rochelle Van Halm told Reuters Placer was not party to any CVG suit for damages.

Placer has, however, filed a counter writ with the Supreme Court against Crystallex's claim, saying that it is based on an erroneous legal interpretation. Crystallex currently has a case with the Supreme Court that it says will enforce an April 15 ruling and give it clear title.

Last week Placer president Carl Gagnier also said in Caracas he had asked the CVG to clarify why title to Las Cristinas was unclear. Gagnier added that environmental permits from the Venezuelan authorities, required before the project could begin, were still pending.
"The whole thing continues to get more and more interesting," Crystallex's Marshall said.
